cards.info: What is the formula for the slope $m$ between two points?
cards.backInfo: The slope formula is $m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)$.

cards.info: What is the relationship between the slopes of two parallel lines?
cards.backInfo: Two non-vertical lines are parallel if and only if their slopes are equal.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing how to determine if lines are parallel or perpendicular based on their slopes.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/ac58d779-57ca-471a-bdaf-6f1fe0b95bcf-1786506045015-779.webp)

cards.info: What is the product of the slopes of two perpendicular lines?
cards.backInfo: The product of the slopes of two perpendicular non-vertical lines is $-1$.

cards.info: What is the slope and general equation form of a horizontal line?
cards.backInfo: A horizontal line has a slope of $0$ and the form $y = k$.

cards.info: What is the slope and general equation form of a vertical line?
cards.backInfo: A vertical line has an undefined slope and the form $x = h$.

cards.info: What is the geometric relationship between any horizontal and vertical line?
cards.backInfo: Every horizontal line is perpendicular to every vertical line in the coordinate plane.

cards.info: How do you identify the slope from a linear equation?
cards.backInfo: Rewrite the equation into slope-intercept form ($y = mx + b$), where $m$ is the slope.

cards.info: What common mistake occurs when finding a perpendicular slope?
cards.backInfo: Failing to change the sign when determining the negative reciprocal of the slope.

cards.info: Why are lines with equal slopes and equal y-intercepts not parallel?
cards.backInfo: They are considered the same (coincident) line rather than parallel lines.

cards.info: How can you verify if two lines are perpendicular using their slopes?
cards.backInfo: Multiply the two slopes together; the result must be exactly $-1$.

cards.info: If you calculate $m = (x2 - x1) / (y2 - y1)$, what error occurred?
cards.backInfo: The coordinates were subtracted in the wrong order; $x$ was placed on top.

cards.info: If Line A has slope $2/3$, what is the slope of parallel Line B?
cards.backInfo: The slope of Line B is $2/3$ because parallel lines have equal slopes.

cards.info: To find a perpendicular slope, what two operations must you perform?
cards.backInfo: Flip the fraction (reciprocal) and change the sign (negative).
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing how to determine if lines are parallel or perpendicular based on their slopes.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/ac58d779-57ca-471a-bdaf-6f1fe0b95bcf-1786506045015-779.webp)

cards.info: What is the slope of the line represented by the equation $y = 5$?
cards.backInfo: The slope is $0$ because it is a horizontal line.

cards.info: Why can't you use the $m1 * m2 = -1$ rule for vertical lines?
cards.backInfo: Vertical lines have an undefined slope, so the product cannot be calculated.

cards.info: Is the line $x = 2$ perpendicular to the line $y = -3$?
cards.backInfo: Yes, because every vertical line is perpendicular to every horizontal line.

cards.info: What is the slope of the line $2x + y = 5$?
cards.backInfo: The slope is $-2$ after rewriting the equation as $y = -2x + 5$.

cards.info: If a student says the perpendicular slope to $4$ is $1/4$, what's missing?
cards.backInfo: The student forgot to change the sign to make it a negative reciprocal.

cards.info: What distinguishes parallel lines from coincident lines in the coordinate plane?
cards.backInfo: Parallel lines have equal slopes but must have different y-intercepts.

cards.info: If a line has a slope of $5$, what is the perpendicular slope?
cards.backInfo: The perpendicular slope is $-1/5$.
